blocks.summary: VLAs lack explicit foresight; WAMs are pixel-expensive; LaWAM uses latent visual subgoals from a 230M LaWM; headline SRs 98.6 LIBERO / 91.22 RoboTwin, 187 ms, 24x lower latency.

VLA limitation (no scene-evolution modeling) and three WAM inefficiencies: pixel synthesis capacity, iterative latency (LingBot-VA 4482 ms vs pi0.5 220 ms), and futures not exposing chunk-relevant state change.

LaWM proposal: latent-action-conditioned dynamics model in frozen DINOv3 feature space; decoder repurposed from LAM; LaWAM two-stage pipeline, 3000h robot + 1500h human video; 2.3B model, 95% fewer world-modeling parameters than 5B WAN.

Three lineages: VLAs with implicit future tokens; pixel-space vs efficiency-oriented WAMs (pi0.7, Fast-WAM, GigaWorld-Policy, LDA-1B); latent action models and the concurrent decoder-as-world-model observation (Garrido et al.).
Eq. (1) WAM decomposition into future prediction and IDM; Eq. (2) LAM posterior and LaWM decoder in frozen feature space; Eq. (3) inference-time factorization policy prior x LaWM x action expert.

Stage 1: LaWM as forward decoder; auxiliary end-effector state predictor g; Eq. (4) forward-prediction + aux + KL objective; physical interval tau makes subgoals correspond to consistent elapsed motion.

Stage 2: policy prior predicts z-hat, LaWM decodes subgoal without pixels; Alternate-DiT action expert with semantic and dynamics streams; Eq. (5) distillation + subgoal supervision + flow matching, with Knowledge Insulation.
Open-source pretraining mixture; policy integration uses only language-annotated robot trajectories; five evaluation axes.
Best average SR 98.6 among VLA/latent-action/WAM baselines; 230M LaWM vs 5B WAN backbone; 187 ms latency, up to 24x faster.
50-task bimanual benchmark; best clean-scene average 92.64, close to strongest pixel-space WAMs under randomization (89.80).
Pick-and-place, drawer opening, towel folding on Franka and Quanta X1; LaWAM best average 90.0 and first on all three tasks; latency-driven baseline failures on towel folding.
Open-loop cross-embodiment rollouts: latent action is embodiment-agnostic, LaWM grounds it in the current latent state; explains why raw latent actions alone are a limited interface.
Removing LaWM causes the largest drop (especially LIBERO-Long); distillation and KI both matter; interface should be driven by aligned latent actions and gradient-protected.
Camera self-motion breaks latent-action coherence (humanoid/mobile robots out of scope); training mixture lacks fine-grained deformable dynamics.
Future prediction as a compact latent interface between semantic instruction following and physically grounded control.
Bibliography [1]-[47]; indexed, not translated line by line.
Per-task RoboTwin success rates expanding Table 2 averages.
Subgoal heatmaps from DINO patch cosine similarity; panels show final frame of each action chunk.
DINOv3 ViT-B/16 features; 24-layer encoder/decoder; V-JEPA2-style encoder; adaLN latent-action conditioning instead of Genie-style additive injection; disposable MLP state heads.
Qwen3-VL first 16 layers; four Alternate-DiT blocks, hidden 1024; query layout with causal mask; EEF actions; no proprioception; RGB 256x256.
Eq. (6) H_b = round(tau h_b); Eq. (7) sinusoidal physical-time encoding phi(t_b,i); shared physical-time coordinate across control frequencies.
Controlled 5/10/20 Hz LIBERO co-training; native 20 Hz as upper-bound reference; physical-time encoding largely recovers performance.

LaWM: 16 H100, 100k steps, AdamW lr 3e-4, batch 1024, beta 1e-5, tau 1.2s robot / 0.4s human, view-decoupled augmentation. Policy: lambda 0.1, 200k steps on 64 H100; 10 denoising steps; latency from 1000 A100 runs; WAM parameter counts exclude VAE/text encoder.

blocks.section: Appendix D.1-D.2 / LIBERO and RoboTwin protocols
blocks.summary: LIBERO: 25k steps, batch 256, 2000 trials over 40 tasks. RoboTwin: 2500 clean + 25000 randomized demos, 100k steps, ~20h on 64 H100, 100 trials per task.
Franka (pick-and-place, drawer) and Quanta X1 (towel); 150/280 demos; 30 trials per task with fixed initial configurations; per-task setups and failure inspection.
